traits: Cap 3 to 12 cm, convex then flat, dark brownish to purplish-grey, covered in thick slime
Gills widely spaced, running down the stem, white then grey, blackening with the spores
Stem 4 to 10 cm, white above, yellow at the base; the veil leaves only an indistinct ring zone, stained by the spores
Whitish flesh, faint smell, mild or slightly acidic taste
Under conifers, often spruce · July to November
safetyNote: Edible once the slime and the skin of the cap are removed: the DGfM and the VAPKO say so, Wikipedia (fr) calls it honourable or mediocre, Wikipedia (en) says opinions differ and that it accumulates heavy metals. Seen from above a young one looks like the slippery jack, but it has gills, not pores (Wikipedia, en); Wikipedia (fr) names Gomphidius maculatus, under larches, as its main look-alike.

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
